stpauls.subtitle: Wren's cathedral · City of London
stpauls.point: Compare the twin western towers with the central dome. From Millennium Bridge, the dome anchors a clear axis through the city.
stpauls.modelNote: OSM building parts combine recorded heights and estimates from storeys. Roofs are simplified.

shard.subtitle: London Bridge
shard.point: Look at the offset glass planes and the open crown. From London Bridge, the river setting emphasises the tower's vertical proportions.
shard.modelNote: An approximate tapered form using the mapped footprint, actual placement and reference height.

gherkin.subtitle: 30 St Mary Axe
gherkin.point: Compare the swelling profile with the diagonal facade grid. Moving through the surrounding narrow streets reveals changing views of its curved form.
gherkin.modelNote: An approximate curved form using the mapped footprint, actual placement and reference height.

towerbridge.subtitle: Tower Bridge Road
towerbridge.point: Compare the upper walkways with the opening bascules below. The south bank offers a view of the suspension structure alongside its Gothic stone towers.
towerbridge.modelNote: OSM building parts combine recorded heights and estimates from storeys. Roofs are simplified.

tate.subtitle: Bankside
tate.point: Compare the power station's long body and chimney with the twisting brick extension behind it. The Turbine Hall shows how industrial space can become a public interior.
tate.modelNote: OSM building parts combine recorded heights and estimates from storeys. Roofs are simplified.

millennium.subtitle: Bankside ↔ City of London
millennium.point: Notice the low suspension structure and the views at pedestrian eye level. The bridge connects Tate Modern and St Paul's along a strong urban axis.
millennium.modelNote: Follows the OSM pedestrian centreline, with an assumed 4 m width and a deck level of 10 m.

barbican.subtitle: Arts centre and residential estate
barbican.point: Look for rough concrete, repeated balconies and raised pedestrian decks. Read the three residential towers, low cultural buildings and water gardens as a city within the city.
barbican.modelNote: OSM building parts combine recorded heights and estimates from storeys. Roofs are simplified.

lloyds.subtitle: 1 Lime Street
lloyds.point: Find the external lifts and service towers. The building makes its working systems part of the street-facing architecture.
lloyds.modelNote: OSM building parts combine recorded heights and estimates from storeys. Roofs are simplified.

westminster.subtitle: Houses of Parliament · Big Ben
westminster.point: Study the repeated riverside facade and contrasting towers. Westminster Bridge brings the long elevation and Elizabeth Tower into one view.
westminster.modelNote: OSM building parts combine recorded heights and estimates from storeys. Roofs are simplified.

abbey.subtitle: Westminster
abbey.architect: Medieval master masons · Nicholas Hawksmoor (west towers)
abbey.point: Follow the long nave, flying buttresses and twin west towers. The medieval body contrasts with the west towers completed in 1745.
abbey.modelNote: OSM building parts combine recorded heights and estimates from storeys. Roofs are simplified.

museum.subtitle: Bloomsbury · Great Court
museum.point: Move from the entrance colonnade into the Great Court. Compare the classical stone perimeter with the light glass roof above the courtyard.
museum.modelNote: OSM building parts combine recorded heights and estimates from storeys. Roofs are simplified.

tower.subtitle: White Tower and fortress
tower.point: Find the central White Tower within successive defensive walls. The riverside setting reveals how the fortress expanded over time.
tower.modelNote: OSM building parts combine recorded heights and estimates from storeys. Roofs are simplified.

isokon.subtitle: Lawn Road Flats · Hampstead
isokon.point: Study the continuous access galleries, rounded ends and compact dwelling proportions. The gallery in the building tells the story of this 1934 experiment in communal living.
isokon.modelNote: Mapped placement and orientation are retained. Four storeys, galleries, parapets, external stairs, rear balconies, the gallery annex and rooftop penthouse are modelled separately. The 2.8 m storey height, details and window spacing are approximated from photographs and heritage records, not measured.

battersea.subtitle: Battersea · Nine Elms
battersea.point: Compare the four chimneys, long turbine halls and central boiler house. From the river, observe the industrial symmetry and the new pedestrian spaces around it.
battersea.modelNote: Uses mapped building parts and the actual positions of four chimneys. Chimneys follow OSM heights with an approximate taper. Fine facade details are omitted.

peckham.subtitle: Peckham Square
peckham.point: Study the projecting, inverted L-shaped reading room and the open square beneath it. Raising the building creates both an entrance and a sheltered public space.
peckham.modelNote: Mapped footprints, the raised reading room (10.5 m underside) and roof elements are retained. Seven leaning supports are a schematic arrangement informed by photographs.

laban.subtitle: Deptford Creek
laban.point: Observe the long facade curving towards the garden and the low, broad proportions. On site, compare the translucent exterior with the theatre enclosed within.
laban.modelNote: Uses the mapped curved footprint and building subdivisions. Translucent cladding and internal spaces are not represented.

canadasquare.subtitle: Canary Wharf
canadasquare.point: Look for the notched square plan and pyramid crown. The surrounding docks and squares frame this vertical landmark.
canadasquare.modelNote: Retains mapped parts, a 235 m total height and the 25 m pyramid crown. Cladding and windows are omitted.

crossrail.subtitle: Canary Wharf · roof garden
crossrail.point: Compare the long building over the dock with its curved canopy. The roof garden continues a pedestrian route above the station and retail spaces.
crossrail.modelNote: Uses the complete mapped footprint and 28 m overall height. The curved canopy section is approximate; its timber lattice, ETFE and interior garden are omitted.

navalcollege.subtitle: Maritime Greenwich
navalcollege.architect: Christopher Wren · Nicholas Hawksmoor and others
navalcollege.point: Compare the paired domes, four courts and colonnades. The open central axis preserves a view from Queen's House to the Thames.
navalcollege.modelNote: Uses the actual footprints, courtyards and mapped parts of four courts. Unrecorded heights and roof forms are approximate; the central viewing axis remains open.

queenshouse.subtitle: Maritime Greenwich
queenshouse.point: Compare the restrained white volumes and the north and south elevations. Notice the axis towards the river between the Naval College buildings and the open park behind.
queenshouse.modelNote: Uses mapped footprints and subdivisions. Unrecorded heights are estimated; windows and ornament are omitted.

observatory.subtitle: Flamsteed House · Greenwich
observatory.point: Find the octagonal observing room, small domes and time ball. The actual site stands on a hill; this atlas uses flat terrain and represents building heights only.
observatory.modelNote: Uses the mapped footprint, roofs and parts of Flamsteed House. Missing heights are estimated. The hill's elevation is not modelled.

nationaltheatre.subtitle: South Bank
nationaltheatre.point: Compare the stacked terraces with the tall stage towers. The riverside walkway connects to public spaces at several levels of the building.
nationaltheatre.modelNote: Uses 21 mapped OSM parts, retaining changes in height between terraces and stage towers. Unrecorded heights are estimated.

festivalhall.subtitle: Southbank Centre
festivalhall.point: Compare the low foyers with the taller central auditorium. The riverside terraces connect public space to the volume of the hall.
festivalhall.modelNote: Uses the mapped outline and taller central auditorium. Heights are estimated from recorded OSM storeys.

hayward.subtitle: Southbank Centre
hayward.point: Look at the concrete galleries, outdoor sculpture terraces and repeated pyramid rooflights. Changes in level shape the exhibition route.
hayward.modelNote: Pyramid rooflights are added above the mapped gallery footprint. Their position, size and height are a schematic arrangement informed by photographs.

britishlibrary.subtitle: St Pancras
britishlibrary.point: Compare the low entrance with the roofs rising deeper into the site. Notice how the brick elevations frame the forecourt.
britishlibrary.modelNote: Stepped roof volumes are added above the actual OSM footprint. Roof divisions and heights are approximate, informed by architectural photographs.

coaldrops.subtitle: King's Cross
coaldrops.point: Observe how the roofs of two long warehouses rise and meet over the central yard. The connection brings the historic industrial buildings together.
coaldrops.modelNote: Uses the mapped warehouses and curved roof outlines. Lifted connecting roofs and the open space below are represented with approximate sections and heights.

aquatics.subtitle: Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park
aquatics.point: Compare the rising and falling roof with the low, open end elevations. The model follows the legacy footprint after removal of the temporary Olympic seating.
aquatics.modelNote: A double-curved roof and overhangs follow the mapped legacy footprint. Sections are approximated using a 45 m reference maximum height. Structure and interiors are omitted.

stpancras.subtitle: Station and former Midland Grand Hotel
stpancras.point: Compare the vast arched train shed with the Gothic hotel facing Euston Road. The engineering span and the richly articulated frontage give the station two distinct architectural identities.
stpancras.architect: William Henry Barlow · George Gilbert Scott
stpancras.modelNote: Uses actual station and hotel footprints. The barrel roof and its transition to the modern extension are approximate. The hotel roofline and 70 m clock-tower profile are schematic, not measured. Fine Gothic ornament, interiors and structural ribs are omitted.

kingscross.subtitle: Euston Road · Western Concourse
kingscross.point: Compare the paired train-shed arches and central clock tower with the sweeping western concourse. The square makes the restrained Victorian frontage easy to read.
kingscross.modelNote: Uses mapped station footprints and parts. Twin train-shed roofs are approximate profiles with a 24 m model height. The western concourse remains a simplified mass; facade arches and detailed roof structure are omitted.

senatehouse.subtitle: University of London · Bloomsbury
senatehouse.point: Follow the stepped stone volumes up to the central tower. The low wings and courtyards emphasise its vertical presence in Bloomsbury.
senatehouse.modelNote: Retains mapped tower setbacks, wings and courtyard footprints. Heights are estimated from OSM storeys rather than a measured elevation; windows and stone details are omitted.

somerset.subtitle: Strand · River Terrace
somerset.point: Walk from the Strand entrance into the central courtyard, then towards the river terrace. Compare the enclosed court with the long, formal elevation facing the Thames.
somerset.modelNote: The mapped courtyard and wings are preserved. The 22 m cornice and raised roof profile are reference-informed assumptions, replacing an incomplete two-storey tag. Windows, columns and ornament are omitted.

nationalgallery.subtitle: Trafalgar Square
nationalgallery.point: Read the long classical facade, central portico and dome from Trafalgar Square. Look at how the entrance and roofline frame the northern edge of the square.
nationalgallery.modelNote: Uses mapped gallery parts, recorded heights, the central dome and portico volumes. Fine columns and ornament are simplified. The neighbouring National Portrait Gallery is not part of this landmark.

bloomberg.subtitle: Walbrook · Bloomberg Arcade
bloomberg.point: Compare the deep facade fins with the public arcade cutting through the site. The low, broad office volumes respond to the surrounding City streets.
bloomberg.modelNote: Uses mapped office volumes and their recorded heights. The arcade footprint is retained. Bronze fins, the interior ramp and underground Roman remains are not modelled.
